title: Prevenient motions are vital operations, not free acts
source_text: C. Itaque motus illos in quibus constituit gratiam praevenientem, censet esse operationes vitales, a facultatibus nostris active procedentes, sed quae tamen libere ab eis non eliciuntur, nec dici debent actus liberi arbitrii, proprie loquendo, quanquam multum a libero arbitrio pendeant. Idque quoniam liberum arbitrium variis modis potest actus illos juvare, vel impedire, eosque desiderare & petere a Deo, & quodammodo seipsum aptare & disponere, ut juxta communem cursum & ordinem divinae providentiae, facilius sibi a Deo donentur.
pass_a_gloss: C. Therefore those motions in which he places prevenient grace, he thinks are vital operations, proceeding actively from our faculties, but which yet are not freely elicited by them, nor ought to be called acts of free choice, properly speaking, although they depend much on free choice. And that because free choice can in various ways help those acts, or hinder them, and desire and ask them from God, & in a certain way fit & dispose itself, that according to the common course & order of divine providence, they be more easily given it by God.
pass_b_english: Thesis C. So he holds that the motions in which he places prevenient grace are vital operations proceeding actively from our faculties. Yet they are not elicited freely by those faculties, and strictly speaking they should not be called acts of free choice, though they depend a great deal on free choice.

The reason is that free choice can help or hinder those acts in various ways, can desire them and ask God for them, and can in some way fit and dispose itself so that, by the common course and order of divine providence, they may be given to it by God more readily.

choices.why: Acts that proceed actively from our faculties, though not freely; scholastic term kept.
